market_context.summary: The day's verified finding is that the Fed is HIKING, read at the source rather than inferred: 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote, the first increase since 2023, with minutes recording inflation risks 'skewed to the upside' and 'not sufficient progress', and a SEP putting end-2026 fed funds at a 4.1 median with a central tendency reaching 4.4. Against that, unemployment has already printed 4.2% for September, above the committee's own 4.1 projection, and August CPI ran +0.40% m/m (~4.9% annualised). That combination — inflation near double target, labour softening, a long end at 5.22% against 3.88% effective funds and a +44bp 10y-2y curve — is a stagflationary tightening, and Robinhood/Kalshi price a December hike at 73-74c against a cut at 1c. It supports banks (a hike on a positive curve expands net interest margin, and Q3 bank earnings open this morning) and real assets, and it condemns credit-financed consumer durables, housing and REITs. No index, VIX or crude level was obtainable this run, so there is no volatility-regime reading behind this summary.

watchlist.instrument: Fed hikes 25bp at the October 2026 FOMC (Kalshi/Robinhood event contract)
watchlist.demotion_reason: The 22% probability floor is a dot count, not a probability, and the cited evidence points at December rather than October.
watchlist.trigger: Re-pitch only on evidence that speaks to the TIMING split between the 10-28 and 12-09 meetings — an on-the-record official pointing at October, a hot September CPI/PCE print before 10-28, or the contract trading materially below 14c without new information. Not on a re-reading of the same SEP table.
watchlist.note: KILLED BY RED TEAM, and it was the book's only conviction 5, so it would have been sized on the strongest claim in the report. The arithmetic is right and the inference drawn from it is not. Central tendency excludes the three highest and three lowest projections, so a central-tendency top equal to the range top (both 4.4) does mean at least four of eighteen participants sit at 4.4 — that step checks out. What does not is treating 4-of-18 as a 22% probability of an October hike. A dot is a participant's preferred rate path, not a draw from a distribution over committee outcomes, and this committee just hiked 12-0 with a median at 4.1 — exactly ONE more hike in 2026. A four-member hawkish minority does not set the October decision, so there is no basis for reading its share as the odds of one. Worse, the one piece of cited evidence that speaks to timing at all points the other way: the minutes say most participants saw another increase as appropriate BY YEAR END, and December is the meeting carrying a SEP to justify a path with. Verified live at 06:40 ET — Oct H25 17/18c against Dec H25 73/74c, so the market prices ~91c of at-least-one-more-hike across the two meetings and agrees with the Fed's own median; it simply allocates the hike to December, which is where the quoted language puts it. The report is right that the Fed is hiking. That is fully priced; what is being bought is the timing, and no evidence here addresses timing. The edge is also inside the noise. Even granting the 22% figure, it is 4 points over an 18c ask in a 1-point-wide market with 1,170,581 contracts of open interest and 2.8M of volume — the most scrutinised macro question in finance, on the venue's most liquid contract. At the market's own 18% the trade is +0.05R before fees, i.e. nothing: the entire published +0.51R expectancy is manufactured by the 26% input, which itself exceeds the report's own 22% floor by four points with no mechanism named for them. Separately, the validation `sources` FAIL on this idea is a false positive — I fetched the Kalshi endpoint and it returns 200.

data_quality_notes:
Research ran 06:00-06:32 ET, inside the pre-open window, and finished with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so this report is not truncated and nothing here is a mid-session view. All equity and ETF prices are the 2026-10-12 close taken with the market closed (age ~14.5h, session 'pre') — that is the freshest honest price at this hour, not stale data. The event-contract price is a live Kalshi last trade at 06:22 ET.

WHAT THE SHAPE OF TODAY IS: six ideas, and four of them are amendments to live or pending positions rather than new risk — the honest result of a day with 17 open positions and 16 unfilled entries, against a new-idea screen that rejected 20+ names. All six are swing. There is NO long_term, intraday, crypto, futures or small-cap idea, and every one of those absences is a documented rejection in notes.md, not missing work: the long_term lane got two deliberate passes (NOC, RTX, AA, WHR, NFLX, LRCX, and a healthcare screen of ELV/MOH/ABT/DHR/TMO/MEDP) and nothing cleared the 2.5 floor against a stated bear-case price; the crypto premise was checked and was simply wrong (IBIT is 5% off a 120-day high, not breaking down); eight small/mid caps with prints inside 10 sessions were screened and all rejected. The report has not been padded to fill those lanes and should not be read as having an oversight in them.

WHY SO MANY REJECTIONS, which is itself a finding: a 2.0 reward-to-risk floor against a 2.0 ATR stop arithmetically demands a target 4+ ATR away. On today's tape that target lands at or above the prior high for names near their highs, and requires reclaiming the moving averages for names in downtrends. GE, CLF, CME, TRV, AZZ and VICR all came out at or just under 2.0 and were dropped rather than nudged.

RATIO CLUSTERING — checked, and partly present: the five equity/ETF ratios run 2.13, 2.16, 2.36, 2.38, 2.58 against a 2.0 floor, and the two closest to it (XLE 2.13, DINO 2.16) are the two whose levels were set at their original entry in August and carried forward unchanged today, so they were not fitted to clear the bar this morning. I recomputed every ratio from the final entry, target and stop rather than trusting the notes, and re-derived each stop in ATRs from freshly fetched OHLCV: 2.13 (DINO, floor 2.0), 2.30 (XLF, 1.8), 2.48 (XLE, 1.8), 2.45 (OXY, 2.0), 2.42 (STLD, 2.0). No ratio in this report is cleared by a tight stop. Conviction equals the distinct evidence-kind count on all six.

ONE LARGE WIN-PROBABILITY CLAIM, flagged rather than hidden: DINO carries 0.70 against a break-even of 0.316, a 38-point claimed edge, past the 20-point line. It is deliberate and I checked the arithmetic rather than accepting it — the position is already +14.3%, its target sits 1.14 ATR above the last close while its stop sits 24.91 away, so the driftless probability of touching the target first measured from spot is 24.91/30.00 = 0.83, which makes 0.70 the conservative number. The baseline validation compares against is computed from the August entry, which is why the edge reads so large. If the red team disagrees, the correction belongs to the probability, not to the levels.

CORRELATION: the energy cluster is at the cap, not over it — XLE, DINO and OXY are three ideas on one driver, which is the maximum config/strategy.md allows, and it is why no fourth energy expression was taken even though energy is the only group making new highs. XLF and the FOMC contract are a second, smaller cluster (two ideas on the Fed path), and they point the same way, so a dovish surprise on 10-28 hurts both.

MECHANICAL NOTE the reader should know: OXY and STLD are both marked WAIT because their entries are conditional (OXY on a pullback into 57.60-59.00, STLD only on a close above 247.10). The publisher holds WAIT ideas out of position tracking, so the stale pending rows they amend — OXY at 54.00 from 09-24 and STLD at 245.50 from 10-10 — will not be rewritten to the corrected levels until an entry actually triggers. The corrected levels are in this report; the tracker still shows the old ones. Separately, three open losers (CCJ, LCII, DAL) are carried on the WATCHLIST as prose rather than as recommendations, because merge_report keys live positions on (symbol, direction) and publishing them as 'sell' would open a second bearish row alongside the long instead of closing it. The honest and mechanically achievable call on all three is 'do not add, let the existing stop work', and their stops sit 1.13 / 0.36 / 0.81 ATR away.

SOURCES THAT FAILED THIS RUN (five, and they bound what the report can claim):
1. No index level, no VIX and no crude price at all. ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, ES and NQ futures, DXY and gold all returned HTTP 429 from Yahoo, and finnhub refuses index CFDs. So there is no volatility-regime reading behind the market context, and the energy thesis (three of six ideas) is built from XLE and three constituents rather than from the commodity it depends on. That is the single biggest gap in this report.
2. scripts/market_data.py events is BROKEN and returned null prices for every market — Kalshi renamed its price fields to a _dollars suffix (yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, last_price_dollars, volume_fp, open_interest_fp) and the parser near scripts/market_data.py:770 still reads yes_bid / yes_ask / last_price / volume / open_interest. Its `search` argument also filters client-side over an arbitrary first 200 open markets, so topical queries return unrelated markets. Worked around by querying series_ticker directly; the rank-1 prices are good. NEEDS A CODE FIX.
3. No options-implied move on ANY idea — Yahoo options returned HTTP 401 (checked for STLD). Nothing in this report has been tested against what the options market prices.
4. Short interest and days-to-cover failed for ALLY, COF and SYF (api.nasdaq.com read timeout), which is part of why the consumer-credit short was rejected rather than published.
5. The federalreserve.gov SEP PDF was unparseable; the HTML projections table was read instead, so the rank-1 dot-distribution argument rests on that. scripts/market_data.py history does not support crypto symbols, so IBIT was used as the bitcoin proxy.
Single-stock quotes, daily OHLCV, FRED, the earnings calendar, insiders, analysts, filings and relative strength all worked.

RED TEAM (phase 2c) — one kill, three downgrades, no level moved.
CUT: KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25, the book's only conviction 5. Its 22% probability floor is a count of dots, not a probability — four of eighteen participants preferring two more hikes does not give a four-member minority 22% of the October decision on a committee that just voted 12-0 with a median at one more hike. The only cited evidence that addresses TIMING ('by year end', plus December being the SEP meeting) points at December, and the Dec/Oct market I re-fetched at 06:40 ET (73/74c vs 17/18c) prices the Fed's own median and allocates it there. The Fed hiking is correct and fully priced; the trade was buying the timing on evidence about the path.
DOWNGRADED: XLF 4 -> 3 and its win probability 0.44 -> 0.34 — the NIM mechanism was tested in public when the Fed hiked on 09-16 and the sector then underperformed SPY by 5.65% over the month; the report's own counter argument concedes it cannot answer this. Hold, do not add. OXY 4 -> 3 — the pending entry was moved up 8% into a name that has run 11.3% in ten sessions, and of its three evidence kinds one is a calendar date and one is a $250k four-month-old insider buy padded with XLE's relative strength, which belongs to another idea in this same book; one real confirmation, not three. DINO 3 -> 2 and 0.70 -> 0.62 — its two evidence items are one OHLCV series from one URL under two labels, and the +1.21R expectancy is a frame artifact: a from-entry 2.16 ratio paired with a from-spot probability. From spot the remaining trade risks 24.91 to make 5.09, so holding is roughly zero expectancy and the trim at 128.00 is the whole idea.
KEPT WITHOUT CHANGE: XLE, now rank 1 — three genuinely distinct evidence kinds, every source resolving, and the only group in the book making new highs. STLD's levels stand: with a 231.50 stop the 2.0 floor needs only a 279.50 target, and 288.74 is the 250-day high, so the 2.58 ratio is not fitted. Its key risk now says the breakout trigger and the 10-19 print may be days apart.
THREE VALIDATION FLAGS I CHECKED AND REJECTED, so the reader does not act on them. (1) The `spread` FAIL on STLD (12.92%) and DINO (11.42%) is an out-of-hours quote artifact, not a real market: STLD's 'bid' of 231.09 is below its own session low of 237.95 and its 'ask' of 263.00 is above the high of 241.63, with the same pattern on DINO (bid 110.20 against a 120.575 low) — both names turn over $227M and $334M a day. If the enforce step demotes them on this, that is a mechanical consequence of pricing at 06:37 with the market shut and not a judgement that either is untradeable. (2) The `earnings_date` warns on OXY, XLF, STLD and DINO are a provider gap, not a bad date: finnhub's calendar now returns nothing between 10-13 and 10-21 (it starts at 10-22), while notes.md records the 06:00 fetch returning JPM/GS/C/WFC for 10-13 and STLD amc 10-19 with four-decimal estimates.
